author: John Harney
description: The Trump administration’s decision to curtail the activities of reporters at the Pentagon, which led to the departure of most news organizations from the building, was blocked on Friday by a federal judge in Washington.
title: Judge Rejects Trump Restrictions on Pentagon Reporters

author: Vincent Lee, Millie Munshi
description: The US Department of Treasury issued a general license allowing the sale of Iranian oil and petrochemical products loaded onto vessels on or before 12:01 am New York time Friday, marking the Trump administration’s latest effort to counter rising oil prices due to the Iran war.
title: US Allows Sale of Stranded Iranian Oil to Cap Energy Price Hikes

author: Jessica Nix, Rachel Cohrs Zhang
description: The Trump administration is closing in on its pick to lead the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, as the nation’s top public health agency grapples with a barrage of attacks and leadership changes in the past year.
title: Trump Administration Nears CDC Pick as Agency Faces Ongoing Leadership Changes

description: Aaron David Miller, Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, says President Trump's recent comments that he's considering "winding down" military operations in the Middle East contradicts expanding deployments and rising risks to global oil flows, warning the conflict is far from over. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: State Department Veteran Questions Iran 'Wind Down'

description: Kevin Book, Managing Director at ClearView Energy Partners, discusses the global oil market impact of disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, the potential for prolonged supply outages and the risk of sharply higher crude and gasoline prices. He also addresses policy options under consideration and implications for US energy strategy. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Kevin Book on Oil Markets, Hormuz Risk, Price Shock

description: Retired Rear Admiral Mark Montgomery discusses the buildup of US forces in the Middle East, the timeline and logistics for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and the role of ground operations. He also addresses reports of a $200 billion supplemental Pentagon funding request and the military capabilities of allies. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ret. Rear Admiral on Gulf Escalation, Hormuz Strategy, Force Posture

author: Caroline Alexander, Fadwa Hodali
description: Hundreds of thousands of people are displaced and huge swathes of land lie in ruins, but Beirut is virtually powerless to protect its people.
title: Israel’s War to Crush Hezbollah Leaves a Weakened Lebanon Near Ruin

author: Caitlin Reilly
description: Americans’ tax refunds are averaging about $350 higher than this time last year but so far running well below the extra $1,000 President Donald Trump promised after passage of his signature economic legislation.
title: Tax Refunds Are Up But Falling Short of Trump’s $1,000 Promise

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: As the public sours on his deportation policies, the president emphasizes law and order.
title: Trump Goes Back to Basics With His Law and Order Message

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss cross-asset volatility to end the week as the Iran war continues with no end in sight. Jeff Mason, White House & Washington Correspondent for Bloomberg, and Adam Farrar, Bloomberg Economics, Senior Geoeconomics Analyst for Asia-Pacific, both join the program to discuss the latest as President Trump faces a dilemma amid rising oil and diesel costs. Then, former Director of Enforcement at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission Ian McGinley joins to discuss Nevada banning Kalshi from operations in the state for now. Plus, Bloomberg News Oil Reporter Nathan Risser weighs in on how rising diesel costs are presenting a new geoeconomic worry. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks, Bonds Fall as No End to War in Sight | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/20/2026

description: President Donald Trump rejects the idea of declaring a cessation of hostilities in Iran, while expressing confidence the Strait of Hormuz would reopen “itself” despite allies’ reluctance to offer assistance. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Rejects Idea of a Ceasefire With Iran

author: Erik Larson
description: The Trump Organization’s lawsuit accusing Capital One Financial Corp. of political discrimination and illegally closing its accounts in 2021 was tossed out by a judge, but he said the claims can be refiled if Trump’s company can fix its “deficient” complaint.
title: Trump Suit Against Capital One Dismissed But Can Be Refiled

author: Jeff Mason, Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump rejected the idea of declaring a cessation of hostilities in Iran, while expressing confidence the Strait of Hormuz would reopen “itself” despite allies’ reluctance to offer assistance.
title: Trump Says He Doesn’t Want Ceasefire in Iran Conflict

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Arbroath Group Managing Partner Christopher Smart, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Bluestack Strategies Founder Maura Gillespie and Cohen Group Senior Advisor Jen Gavito. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Regime Digs In on Hormuz | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/20/2026

author: Bruce Einhorn
description: The Iranian space program, one of the most advanced in the Middle East, has suffered extensive damage from US and Israeli airstrikes, potentially driving Tehran to deepen cooperation with China and Russia.
title: War’s Airstrikes Cripple Iranian Rocket and Satellite Programs

author: Ben Bartenstein, Jennifer A Dlouhy, Courtney McBride
description: US officials say the White House is sending hundreds of Marines to the Middle East as it weighs a plan to seize Iran’s Kharg Island oil export hub. Deploying even a small number of troops on the ground in Iran carries huge risks for President Donald Trump.
title: Trump Risks Dragging Out Iran War With Debate Over Seizing Kharg Island

author: Daniela Milanese, Mariana Durao
description: Brazil President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said he spoke with Mexican leader Claudia Sheinbaum about a possible exploration partnership between their nations’ state-run oil companies in the Gulf of Mexico.
title: Lula Says Petrobras, Pemex Could Partner on Oil Exploration

description: Republican sheriffs in Florida are walking back from Trump's aggressive immigration enforcement. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Mary Ellen Klas explains why. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why Florida Sheriffs Are Pivoting on Immigration

description: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre says Canada has real trade leverage over the US and should use that to their advantage. He talks about how he'd handle negotiations with President Donald Trump in an interview with Bloomberg This Weekend anchor David Gura. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Canada Has Trade Leverage Over the US, Says Opposition Leader Poilievre

author: Oscar Medina
description: The war in the Middle East is a “major threat” to a Colombian economy, which already faced serious price pressures, according to a senior policymaker.
title: Central Banker Sees ‘Major Threat’ to Colombia From Iran War

author: Donato Paolo Mancini, Andrea Palasciano, Gerry Doyle
description: The Iranian regime isn’t close to falling and officials are coalescing around the remaining leaders, according to western intelligence assessments and people familiar with the matter.
title: Iran’s Government Seen as Tightening Grip Despite Strikes

author: Brian Platt, David Gura
description: Canada has real trade leverage with US President Donald Trump and should use it to remove tariffs and deepen ties between the two nations, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said.
title: Poilievre Says Canada Can Use Oil, Minerals to Sway Trump on Tariffs

author: Alex Longley, Grant Smith, Rong Wei Neo
description: Three weeks into the Iran war, there’s an ever-growing gap between the price of oil futures and supplies that determine costs for consumers in the real world.
title: The Oil Prices You See Don’t Tell the Market’s Real Story

author: Ella Feldman
description: A tanker carrying a cargo of diesel believed to be bound for Cuba updated its destination to Trinidad and Tobago shortly after the US clarified that the communist-run island remains ineligible to receive Russian fuel.
title: Tanker of Russian Fuel Veers Away From Cuba as US Tweaks Rules

description: President Donald Trump says Iran has no leaders left. Speaking at the White House, Trump says the US wants to talk to Iran, but adds there’s nobody to talk to. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran's Leaders 'Are All Gone'

author: Samy Adghirni, Ewa Krukowska, Irina Vilcu
description: Iranian officials have become reluctant to even discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz as they focus on surviving the US-Israeli onslaught, according to a person involved in direct, high-level contacts with Tehran.
title: Iran Unwilling to Talk About Opening Hormuz While Under Attack

author: Andrea Palasciano, Max Ramsay
description: NATO’s non-combat advisory mission in Iraq relocated all its personnel from the Middle East to Europe for safety reasons amid the Persian Gulf conflict and after the US signaled waning interest, according to a person familiar with the decision.
title: NATO’s Iraq Mission Relocates Its Staff to Europe for Security

author: Zoltan Simon
description: US Vice President JD Vance will pay a visit to Hungary before the country’s pivotal April 12 elections, Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto told a podcast.
title: US Vice President to Visit Hungary Before Vote, Szijjarto Says

author: Matthew Bristow
description: The US Justice Department is investigating Colombian President Gustavo Petro for possible ties to drug traffickers, the New York Times reported.
title: US Probes Colombia President for Alleged Narco Ties, NYT Reports

author: Olivia Raimonde
description: Citing concerns about affordability, New York Governor Kathy Hochul has proposed revising the state’s 2019 climate law, asking to delay regulations to implement it and to adopt a different greenhouse-gas accounting method.
title: Hochul Moves to Weaken Aggressive New York State Climate Law

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump denounced NATO as “COWARDS,” ratcheting up his rhetoric against the military alliance over its refusal to help the US reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway blocked since the start of the Iran war.
title: Trump Calls NATO ‘Cowards’ for Not Helping Join Fight With Iran

description: Schwab Asset Management CEO and CIO Omar Aguilar talks about how clients are positioning themselves as war risks linger. He says risk aversion has been "increasing dramatically" for the last few weeks. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Risk Aversion Has Been 'Increasing Dramatically', Schwab's Aguilar Says

author: Greg Ryan
description: Residents exiting Massachusetts took a net of $4.2 billion in adjusted gross income with them in 2023, one of the largest totals in the country, after a tax on millionaires took effect.
title: Massachusetts Lost $4 Billion of Income After Millionaire Tax

author: Ari Natter, Will Wade
description: SoftBank Group Corp. is working to build a massive AI data center on federally owned land in Ohio that it’s planning to power with roughly $33 billion worth of natural gas-fired electricity to be installed by the end of the decade.
title: SoftBank Plans Giant Ohio AI Data Center Powered by Gas Plants

author: Martha Viotti Beck, Felipe Saturnino
description: The Brazilian Treasury’s record interventions in local markets are eating into a liquidity cushion seen as key to managing public debt risks.
title: Treasury’s Record Interventions Challenge Brazil Financing Plan

author: Zoe Tillman, Janet Lorin
description: The Justice Department sued Harvard University for allegedly violating Jewish students’ civil rights in the Trump administration’s latest attack on the university.
title: Harvard Sued by DOJ Over Alleged Antisemitism on Campus

author: Olesia Safronova, Aliaksandr Kudrytski
description: Ukraine’s negotiators will discuss a potential drone deal with the US when they meet for talks on Saturday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.
title: Kyiv Will Raise Drone Deal Offer in US Talks, Zelenskiy Says

author: Nojoud Al Mallees
description: As tighter immigration policies bring population growth to a halt, more than half of Canadians say the country should allow even fewer new immigrants and temporary residents in 2027 compared to this year.
title: Canadians Want Lower Immigration Even as Population Growth Stalls

author: Nathan Risser, Ella Feldman, Will Kubzansky
description: No one can stop talking about sky-high gasoline prices. The ripple effects of diesel are worth watching too.
title: Why Diesel Prices Are the Real Concern for the Economy

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump released a national framework for regulating artificial intelligence on Friday, laying the groundwork for Congress to create a federal standard for the rapidly growing technology.
title: White House Unveils AI Legislative Plan for Skeptical Congress

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: Spain’s government has approved a €5 billion ($5.8 billion) aid package to ease the economic effects of the Iran war, including tax reductions on energy.
title: Spain Announces €5 Billion Aid Package to Curb Iran War Impact

author: Lucca de Paoli, Constantine Courcoulas, Donal Griffin
description: Market Financial Solutions Limited, the mortgage lender that collapsed last month, was hit with an investigation by the UK financial watchdog.
title: UK Probes Collapsed MFS as Backers Hunt for Missing Billions

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russia is moving to allow the use of its armed forces to protect citizens facing arrest or prosecution overseas, underscoring Moscow’s hostility toward foreign courts pursuing cases against Russians.
title: Russia Plans to Allow Military to Defend Citizens Prosecuted Abroad

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Switzerland will temporarily stop exports linked to any new US arms and ammunition orders, citing its tradition of neutrality amid the Iran war.
title: Swiss Ban Arms Exports to US During Iran War Over Neutrality

author: Eric Martin
description: The Trump administration is reorganizing foreign aid at a fraction of its former size after dismantling USAID, a move critics say has cost millions of lives.
title: Trump Reorganizes Foreign Aid at Fraction of USAID’s Size

author: Rodrigo Orihuela, Donato Paolo Mancini, Alberto Brambilla
description: Italy is in talks with Algeria to buy more natural gas from the North African nation with the Iran war squeezing energy shipments, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Italy Joins Race for Algerian Gas With Iran War Cutting Supplies

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: Spain’s government is set to announce on Friday cuts on fuel and electricity taxes as part of a broad aid package to counter the surge in energy prices due to the war in the Middle East, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Spain to Cut Fuel, Electricity Taxes in Economic Relief Package

author: Golnar Motevalli
description: Israel’s attack on a key Iranian gas field may have jolted all sides into dialing back the war’s destructive potential.
title: Have All Sides in the Iran War Just Blinked?

description:
"Spending $2 billion a day in Iran is an extraordinary waste of resources."

California Representative Ro Khanna tells Mishal Husain that Donald Trump is facing growing pressure over the Iran war, including from his own supporters. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Anti-War Democrat Courting MAGA Voters

description: India has friends everywhere but leverage nowhere, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Mihir Sharma says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: India's Strategy Is Hurting It With Iran

author: Miaojung Lin
description: Taiwan said it will skip a WTO conference in Cameroon due to a dispute over how the hosts labeled its delegation in visa paperwork.
title: Taiwan to Skip WTO Meeting Due to Visa Dispute With Cameroon

author: Josh Sisco
description: Nvidia Corp.’s $20 billion licensing deal with artificial intelligence startup Groq is being probed by a pair of Democratic senators over whether it violates antitrust laws by improperly avoiding a merger review and illegally consolidating its power in the market for AI computing.
title: Nvidia’s $20 Billion Groq Deal Queried by Warren, Blumenthal

author: Kamlesh Bhuckory
description: Mauritius Deputy Prime Minister Paul Bérenger resigned after complaining that his warnings of threats to the Indian Ocean nation’s economy were being ignored.
title: Mauritius Deputy PM Resigns, Says his Economic Warnings Ignored

author: Ignacio Olivera Doll, Ken Parks
description: Empresarios latinoamericanos llegan en masa, elegantes torres se elevan sobre la antes adormecida capital y su presidente conservador estrecha vínculos con EE.UU.
title: El milagro de Paraguay: de país ignorado a imán de inversiones

author: Ignacio Olivera Doll, Ken Parks
description: Entrepreneurs flock to Paraguay from across the region as sleek towers rise above the once-sleepy capital and its conservative president cozies up to the US.
title: An Underdog Trump Ally in Latin America Becomes an Investor Magnet

author: Paul Tugwell
description: Cyprus wants a “frank, open discussion,” with the UK government over the future of the British sovereign bases on the eastern Mediterranean island when the current conflict in the Middle East is over, the nation’s President said.
title: Cyprus President Calls for Talks With UK On Sovereign Bases

description:
On today's show, Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel would avoid attacks on Iran’s energy infrastructure, and added that the war will end a lot faster than people think as Tehran is no longer able to enrich uranium or manufacture ballistic missiles.

Oil declined after the US and Israel sought to calm investors shaken by serious damage to key Gulf energy assets.

European Union leaders have been unable to break a deadlock over a €90 billion loan to Ukraine. The Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is refusing to budge until he regains access to Russian oil, leaving European leaders frustrated.

Today's guests: Swiss Re Chief Europe Economist Charlotte Mueller & W1M Head of UK Equity Research Tineke Frikkee. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Israel Says It Won’t Strike Iran Energy Sites After Trump Rebuke | Daybreak Europe 3/20/2026

description: Israel said it launched a wave of strikes overnight targeting infrastructure across Tehran, while Iran struck Kuwait’s Mina Al-Ahmadi oil refinery for a second day. On Thursday US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sought to ease concerns about rising oil and gas prices following tit-for-tat Israeli and Iranian attacks on key energy facilities. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Strikes Continue as Trump, Netanyahu Try to Ease Concern

author: Patrick Sykes, Kateryna Kadabashy
description: Iran pressed ahead with attacks on Arab states in the Persian Gulf even after Israel signaled it would refrain from hitting the Islamic Republic’s energy infrastructure, fueling volatility in markets roiled by the war in the oil-rich region.
title: Iran Keeps Striking Gulf as Israel Pledges to Spare Energy Sites

description:
Despite a Pearl Harbor jibe from President Donald Trump, PM Sanae Takaichi showed Japan’s deep ties with the US — and her own agility on the world stage — during her first visit to Washington as a national leader.

Alastair Gale has more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Takaichi Navigates Trump's Pearl Harbor Jibe in DC Visit

author: Tom Rees
description: Britain borrowed more than forecast in February, boosted by a surge in debt-interest costs even before turmoil hit bond markets following the outbreak of war in the Middle East.
title: UK Posts Bigger-Than-Forecast Budget Deficit on Debt Costs

description: Damage following an Iranian strike in Tel Aviv, on March 19. Photographer: Erik Marmor/Getty Images
title: Iran Continues Gulf Strikes After Israel Vows to Spare Energy Sites

description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen accused Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban of "not honoring his word" after EU leaders failed to break the deadlock over a €90 billion ($103 billion) loan to Ukraine. Orban, backed by Slovakia, is refusing to unlock the aid until Hungary regains access to Russian oil. Several leaders say Orban's stance amounts to a breach of an agreement among EU nations in December. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: EU Says Orban 'Not Honoring His Word' on Ukraine Loan Deal

description: Congressman Ro Khanna of California helped force the Epstein Files release. He tells Mishal Husain why opposing the Iran war and taxing billionaires can unite progressives and wavering Trump voters. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Anti-War Democrat Courting MAGA Voters

author: Jan Bratanic
description: Slovenia is heading into a tight election on Sunday as top contenders in the race trade accusations over a scandal involving alleged foreign interference in the campaign.
title: Foreign Meddling Scandal Turns Slovenia Election Into a Toss-Up

author: Alastair Gale
description: Sanae Takaichi had warned her first summit with Donald Trump in Washington could be “extremely difficult,” after the US asked her to deploy warships to Iran. Instead, she showcased Japan’s deep ties with the US — and her own agility on the world stage.
title: Takaichi Evades Iran Spat With Trump Despite Pearl Harbor Jibe

author: Jenny Leonard, Arne Delfs
description: In the exhibition hall at Unitree Robotics in Hangzhou, Friedrich Merz smiled and applauded the martial arts display by a platoon of humanoid warriors. But when a robot boxer advanced toward him, punching the air with its red-gloved fists, the German chancellor flinched, a look of alarm crossing his face as he appeared to realize the danger posed by an autonomous fighting machine.
title: Chaos Unleashed by Trump Has Europeans Building Bridges With China

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: North Korea unveiled new battle tanks that it claimed were capable of blocking missiles and drone attacks as leader Kim Jong Un urged the military to step up war preparations, state media reported.
title: Kim Jong Un and Daughter Unveil New Tank to Repel Drones

author: Josh Xiao
description: A mystery craft has been spotted in China resembling a vehicle designed to avoid radar by flying just a few meters above the sea, suggesting Beijing may be experimenting with a Soviet-era model the US shelved last year.
title: Sea-Skimming Craft Spotted as China Expands its Naval Ambitions

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sen. Gary Peters of Michigan, Ranking Member of the Senate Homeland Security Committee and member of the Armed Services Committee, discusses the prospect of a $200 billion supplemental request from the Pentagon. Cuba Ambassador to the UN, Ernesto Soberon Guzman, talks about President Trump's remarks about Cuba. Former US Defense Secretary Leon Panetta addresses the potential need for sustained military presence, including air and possible ground operations, and the broader economic and political implications of the Middle East conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pentagon Seeks $200B From Congress For Iran Conflict | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/19/2026

author: John Ainger, Ewa Krukowska, Donato Paolo Mancini
description: The European Union is bracing for a protracted energy price shock after Iran crippled a vital Qatar gas plant, raising the prospect of a years-long supply crunch.
title: EU Leaders Confront Multi-Year Energy Squeeze After Qatar Hit

author: Ashleigh Furlong
description: England’s drug price regulator will reconsider its decision to rule out using Eli Lilly & Co.’s Alzheimer’s disease treatment — and another made Eisai Co. and Biogen Inc. — in the state-run National Health Service, following successful appeals by the companies.
title: England to Review Rejection of Alzheimer’s Drugs for NHS
